answer: Behavioral clustering stops Sybils by grouping identities whose work patterns match too closely. Each fake must sustain its own distinct rhythm of timing, task choice, and reasoning style, checked against the population; one copied pattern cannot serve many clones, because near-identical histories fall into the same cluster and lose weight together. An operator cannot velvet over the gap: the canyon between independent histories and mass-produced ones shows in repeated phrasing and synchronized timing, and a cluster caught sharing answers is pushed off the ledge of eligibility entirely.
